Article Title: 'Drugs take families, careers to new low': PM Modi launches 'Nasha Mukt Yuva' campaign - top quotes
Article Text:
PM Modi virtually launches 'Nasha Mukt Yuva' campaign (File photo)

Here are the top quotes from his address:

Youth must stay fit for developed India

"Today, all countrymen have come together for a great and important resolve. The campaign we are witnessing is meant for individuals, families and society, but above all, it is for the nation. The campaign, 'Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat', clearly reflects this resolve. As the country moves towards the goal of a developed India, it is essential that our youth remain physically and mentally healthy and stay away from drugs and other such harmful substances."

"The campaign we are witnessing today is for the individual, the family, and society; above all, it is for the nation. The very name of this movement—the 'Drug-Free Youth' initiative under the Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan — clarifies its resolve. As the nation sets its sights on becoming a Viksit Bharat, it is essential that our youth be healthy in body and mind, brimming with self-confidence, and forever free from the deadly habit of drugs. This is the objective of the campaign... This campaign was launched last year as a pilot project from Kashi... Over 125 spiritual organizations have joined us today for the welfare of crores of our fellow citizens."

"By being addiction-free, you need to protect your potential. You need to be aware that drugs get you high for a short time, but take your career and family to a new low/bottom.

From Varanasi to nationwide campaign

"As the MP from Kashi, I am happy that this campaign was launched last year from the sacred land of Kashi as a pilot project. Along with scientific clarity, it also carries spiritual energy. Social organisations and NGOs have joined this initiative for the welfare of crores of Indians. Together, they have prepared a roadmap through the Kashi Declaration. Today, we are witnessing how the welfare-oriented idea that emerged from Kashi has become a national project. From today, the Nasha Mukt Yuva campaign is being launched across the country."

"The 'Nasha Mukta Yuva Abhiyaan' is launching across the country today... There is immense power in collective action, and today, driven by that very strength, this campaign is set to touch the heart of every young person. NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday launched the 'Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan', calling on the country's youth to stay physically and mentally fit and remain away from drug abuse.He said achieving the goal of a developed India requires a healthy, confident and drug-free younger generation. He added that the next 100 Sundays would represent 100 strong steps towards a drug-free India."Next 100 Sundays will mark 100 strong steps towards drug-free India," he said.The 'Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan' aims to encourage young people to stay away from substance abuse and become ambassadors of positive social change in their communities.The launch marks the beginning of a 100-week nationwide Jan Bhagidari campaign, under which awareness programmes will be organised every Sunday across the country.Activities will include sports events, walkathons, meditation sessions, cultural programmes, street plays, discussions, art competitions and community engagement initiatives.The campaign brings together educational institutions, youth organisations, civil society groups, industry bodies and more than 125 spiritual organisations to build a collective movement against substance abuse.Youth from over 10,000 locations across the country are participating through schools, colleges, universities, MY Bharat volunteers, NSS volunteers, youth clubs, NGOs and industry associations.

Article Title: 'Dismantle terror infrastructure first': India's US envoy hits out at Pakistan over Indus Waters Treaty
Article Text:

India’s envoy to the US, Vinay Mohan Kwatra said Pakistan had eroded the foundation of the Indus Waters Treaty over the past five decades. He added that Islamabad had “dismantled” the goodwill and friendship that underpinned the 1960 agreement, and that New Delhi’s decision to keep the treaty in abeyance merely acknowledged that reality.As reported by US' Newsweek magazine, Kwatra said the treaty’s preamble reflected a commitment made 'in a spirit of goodwill and friendship', but Pakistan’s conduct had weakened that foundation over half a century.“It is worth remembering that the treaty's preamble declares it was concluded ‘in a spirit of goodwill and friendship’. Pakistan spent half a century dismantling that goodwill and friendship. The abeyance merely acknowledges what Pakistan's conduct had already destroyed,” Kwatra said.His remarks came after Pakistan recently hosted a conference protesting India’s decision to keep the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) in abeyance on April 23 last year, a day after Pakistan-trained terrorists killed 26 people in Pahalgam, Jammu and Kashmir.The IWT, signed by India and Pakistan in 1960, divided the waters of the six rivers of the Indus basin between the two countries. India was given control over the eastern rivers, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej which account for about 20 per cent of the basin’s water, while Pakistan received rights over the western rivers Indus, Jhelum and Chenab carrying around 80 per cent.“That asymmetry stifled development for decades in Indian regions that could have benefited from better water rights. India honoured the treaty anyway,” Kwatra said according to Newsweek.The envoy said Pakistan’s approach towards India had been marked by wars, hostility and cross-border terrorism, citing the 1965, 1971 and 1999 conflicts along with major terror attacks, including the 2001 Parliament attack, the 2008 Mumbai attacks, the 2016 Uri and Pathankot attacks, the 2019 Pulwama attack and the 2025 Pahalgam attack.Kwatra also said that if Pakistan sincerely wanted India’s cooperation on bilateral issues, it must first dismantle the terror infrastructure it has built over the years.On implementation of the treaty, Kwatra alleged that Pakistan had repeatedly delayed Indian projects and opposed efforts to revisit the agreement in view of changing technology and requirements.“Pakistan also consistently blocked India's initiatives to renegotiate the treaty in light of six decades of technological change, which would have let India develop its hydropower potential,” Kwatra added.“Bit by bit, Pakistan eroded India's faith that it could exercise its rights under the treaty, or hope for a better one suited to today's realities,” he said.Responding to calls for India and Pakistan to resume talks, Kwatra said past initiatives had failed to address core concerns.“Prime Minister Narendra Modi has clearly voiced India’s stand today: ‘Terror and talks cannot go together... Terror and trade cannot go together... Water and blood cannot flow together',” Kwatra said.Kwatra also said Pakistan should focus on improving its own water management instead of blaming India for its challenges."The Government of Pakistan would do better to fix its dismal water productivity, than to stage conferences blaming India and issuing threats,” he said, adding, “The habit of pinning every domestic failure on India has grown old."
Article Summary: India’s envoy to the US, Vinay Mohan Kwatra said Pakistan had eroded the foundation of the Indus Waters Treaty over the past five decades. He added that Islamabad had ‘dismantled’ the goodwill and friendship that underpinned the 1960 agreement. The IWT, signed by India and Pakistan in 1960, divided the waters of the six rivers of theindus basin.

NEW DELHI: Want to age more slowly? The answer may lie not just in exercise and diet, but also in a trip to the theatre, museum or even the cinema.A new study by Japanese researchers has found that older adults who engage more frequently in cultural activities tend to have a lower physiological age—a measure of how well the body's organs and systems are functioning—than their actual age, suggesting cultural engagement may be an overlooked tool for healthy ageing.Researchers from the Institute of Science Tokyo analysed 4,207 observations from 1,899 adults aged 50 years and above in the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing. Participants who more frequently visited cinemas, museums, art galleries, theatres, concerts or the opera had lower physiological age. Every one-point increase in cultural engagement score was associated with a 0.085-year reduction in physiological age, even after adjusting for income, health status, employment, smoking, physical activity and other factors. The association persisted in a four-year follow-up analysis. Physiological age, estimated using 10 markers including blood pressure, lung function, grip strength, walking speed, BMI, haemoglobin, cholesterol and blood sugar, is considered a better predictor of disease and mortality than chronological age.The researchers said cultural engagement may promote healthy ageing by strengthening social connections, reducing loneliness and stress, improving mental well-being and encouraging healthier lifestyles.Indian experts said the findings reinforce the importance of staying socially engaged as people age.Dr Prasun Chatterjee, Group Clinical Lead, Department of Geriatric Medicine and Longevity Sciences, Apollo Hospitals, and former professor at AIIMS, said the findings reinforce that healthy ageing depends not only on diet and exercise but also on social and cultural engagement. Social interaction improves memory and mood by boosting serotonin and dopamine, enhancing emotional well-being, memory and a sense of purpose, which encourage healthier lifestyles. In the Indian context, he said, activities such as visiting parks, cinemas, theatres or places of worship can provide similar benefits by promoting happiness, social connection and purpose.Prof Rajesh Sagar, psychiatrist at AIIMS, New Delhi, said social and cultural engagement promotes healthy ageing by strengthening emotional support networks, improving cognitive function and reducing chronic stress.He said loneliness increases the risk of depression, anxiety and cognitive decline while reducing motivation for physical activity. Article Title: Global breastfeeding rates rise, India yet to arrest decline
Article Text:
File photo

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Even as exclusive breastfeeding rates have improved globally over the past decade, India continues to lag behind, with the proportion of infants exclusively breastfed for the first six months declining from 63.7% in NFHS-5 (2019-21) to 55.8% in NFHS-6 (2023-24).Ahead of World Breastfeeding Week (August 1-7), the World Health Organization (WHO) and UNICEF called for stronger support systems for mothers, saying global exclusive breastfeeding has increased from about 37% in 2012 to over 47% today, driven by sustained investments in health systems, community counselling and maternity protection. However, the agencies said progress remains uneven and many countries continue to fall short of global targets.Responding to a question in the Rajya Sabha, the Union health ministry attributed the decline in India's exclusive breastfeeding rate to multiple factors, including socio-cultural practices, family customs, individual preferences, the use of pre-lacteal feeds and infant milk substitutes, and breastfeeding frequency.The ministry, however, highlighted improvements in other breastfeeding indicators.Early initiation of breastfeeding within one hour of birth increased from 41.8% to 50.1%, while the proportion of infants below six months receiving any breast milk rose marginally from 95.1% to 95.6%.The Rajya Sabha question had sought to know whether the government had assessed the impact of rising Caesarean deliveries, inadequate postnatal lactation counselling and early return to work, particularly among women in the informal sector. While the ministry did not provide findings of any such assessment, it said the National Health Mission promotes exclusive breastfeeding through the Mother Absolute Affection (MAA) programme, lactation management centres, healthcare worker training, Poshan Tracker-based counselling and community awareness campaigns.It also cited a 2025 NITI Aayog evaluation, which found that new mothers were receiving information on exclusive breastfeeding during the postnatal period.Calling breastfeeding one of the most effective public health interventions, WHO and UNICEF said it provides essential nutrition, protects children against infections, strengthens immunity, supports cognitive development and lowers mothers' risk of breast and ovarian cancers and type 2 diabetes. The agencies said scaling up proven interventions, including skilled breastfeeding support, community counselling, paid maternity leave, supportive workplace policies and stronger regulation of breast-milk substitute marketing, could prevent nearly 400,000 child deaths and 140,000 maternal deaths globally every year.
Article Summary: The proportion of infants exclusively breastfed for the first six months has declined from 63.7% in 2019-21 to 55.8% in 2023-24. The Union health ministry attributed the decline in India's exclusive breastfeeding rate to multiple factors.

NEW DELHI: Long and crushing working hours have become a serious challenge for resident doctors, causing them psychological distress and mental health problems. Flagging the issue in an affidavit before Supreme Court, National Medical Commission (NMC) has stressed that reasonable working hours and time for rest are a must for their wellbeing and proper functioning, as well as proper patient care. It, however, expressed its inability to ensure the same, saying the matter falls within the domain of central and state health authorities.In the affidavit filed in response to a PIL by a group of doctors seeking healthy working conditions, the commission placed the findings of its task force, which had projected a grim picture of what doctors have to endure.“The demanding schedules, including long and multiple 24-hour duties (sometimes 3-5 consecutive duties), were significant stressors for most post graduate doctors. These extended hours without adequate rest led to physical and mental exhaustion, negatively impacting their performance and health,” commission said, referring to the report.Doctors’ organisation ‘United Doctors Front’ had approached the court demanding healthy working conditions, pointing out that cases of doctors’ suicides are on the rise and claiming that 150 such cases have been reported in five years.
Article Summary: Long and crushing working hours have become a serious challenge for resident doctors. NEW DELHI: The death toll in Friday night's terror attack on migrant labourers in Jammu and Kashmir's Kulgam rose to two on Saturday after a Chhattisgarh worker succumbed to injuries in hospital, officials told news agency PTI.The attack took place late Friday night in the Kelam area of south Kashmir, where the two workers were employed at a brick kiln. Officials said both men sustained critical injuries after terrorists fired at them.One of the labourers, identified as Deepak Ratray, died before he could be shifted to a hospital. The second victim, Bopinder, was initially admitted to Government Medical College (GMC) Anantnag before being referred to SKIMS Hospital in Soura, where he later succumbed to his injuries.Officials said both victims were in their twenties and had travelled from Chhattisgarh in search of work.The incident comes days after terrorists shot dead Jammu and Kashmir Police head constable Ashiq Hussain Qureshi at Anantnag's Lal Chowk while he was deployed on Amarnath Yatra duty. That attack, on July 22, was the first terror strike in Kashmir since the April 22, 2025 Pahalgam massacre, in which 26 people were killed.Friday's attack has also revived concerns over the safety of migrant workers in the Valley. In February 2024, two non-local labourers from Punjab, Amritpal Singh and Rohit Masih, were shot dead in Srinagar. Before that, in October 2021, terrorists killed two workers from Bihar, Raja Reshi Dev and Joginder Reshi Dev, in Kulgam's Wanpoh area.Lieutenant governor Manoj Sinha condemned the latest attack and said security forces had been instructed to intensify anti-terror operations."I strongly condemn this cowardly act. I have directed our security forces to step up their operations and eliminate the terrorists," Sinha wrote on X, adding that he had spoken to DGP Nalin Prabhat and other senior security officials.PDP president and former chief minister Mehbooba Mufti also condemned the killings."They work themselves to the bone far away from home only to feed their families. Unimaginably cruel to target them in such senseless acts of violence," she said.BJP's Jammu and Kashmir spokesperson Altaf Thakur described the attack as "cowardly, barbaric and inhuman", alleging that its objective was to disturb peace and normalcy in the Union Territory.The attack occurred during the ongoing Amarnath Yatra, which began on July 3. While the pilgrimage through the Pahalgam route has remained suspended since July 19 because of heavy rain and landslides, the Baltal route in Ganderbal continues to remain operational.Following the attack, security forces launched a cordon-and-search operation in the area to trace those responsible.
Article Summary: The attack took place late Friday night in the Kelam area of south Kashmir. One of the labourers, identified as Deepak Ratray, died before he could be shifted to a hospital. The second victim, Bopinder, was initially admitted to Government Medical College before being referred to SKIMS Hospital in Soura.

NEW DELHI: A 52-year-old BSF constable who recently returned from the Democratic Republic of Congo as part of an Indian UN peacekeeping contingent has been admitted to the isolation ward at the Ebola Nursing Home of Dr Ram Manohar Lohia (RML) Hospital after developing fever during mandatory quarantine, triggering Ebola surveillance protocols.The constable, who arrived in India on July 11, had been under a 21-day quarantine at the Airport Health Organisation (APHO) facility following his return from Congo, an Ebola-endemic region. On the evening of 20th day of quarantine, he developed a fever along with body aches.As per protocol, he was shifted to the designated Ebola isolation facility at RML Hospital. His blood sample has been sent to the National Institute of Virology (NIV), Pune, for confirmatory testing. The test report is awaited.Officials said the patient is being managed in strict isolation while health authorities continue to monitor the situation. At present, the case remains suspected, and Ebola infection has not been confirmed.India follows enhanced screening and quarantine measures for personnel returning from Ebola-affected regions. Suspected cases are isolated immediately and samples are tested at designated reference laboratories before a diagnosis is confirmed.
Article Summary: A 52-year-old BSF constable has been admitted to the isolation ward at the Ebola Nursing Home of Dr Ram Manohar Lohia (RML) Hospital. NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday inaugurated the Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport at Bhogapuram in Andhra Pradesh 's Vizianagaram district, a nearly Rs 5,000 crore project that the state government says will transform North Andhra into a major economic and industrial hub. Calling the airport a key milestone in the state's growth story, the PM said the NDA government was working at "double speed"for the state's development.During his address, the Prime Minister also took a veiled swipe at the Gandhi family, saying airports in the past were often named after "a single family". He said the NDA government had instead chosen to honour national icons by naming airports after figures such as Valmiki, Sant Ravidas and Alluri Sitarama Raju.The PM was accorded a grand ceremonial welcome, with around 13,500 tribal women performing the traditional Dhimsa dance. The airport premises were adorned with displays celebrating Andhra Pradesh's rich cultural heritage, including Etikoppaka artwork and motifs depicting the state's geographical identity.PM Modi was received by Andhra Pradesh chief minister N Chandrababu Naidu, deputy chief minister Pawan Kalyan, and union civil aviation minister K Ram Mohan Naidu.He later witnessed the Dhimsa performance before formally inaugurating the airport.Developed by the GMR Group, the airport has been named after freedom fighter Alluri Sitarama Raju. It has been designed to handle six million passengers annually in its first phase, with a long-term expansion plan to increase capacity to 40 million passengers a year. Commercial flight operations are scheduled to begin on August 17.Also Read: PM Modi inaugurates Rs 5,640-crore Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport in Andhra Pradesh — See pics The Andhra Pradesh government has projected the airport as a key catalyst for industrial growth, employment generation, exports, skill development and improved connectivity across North Andhra.Following the inauguration, chief minister Naidu felicitated PM Modi with a traditional shawl before he laid the foundation stone, inaugurated and dedicated multiple development projects worth over Rs 17,900 crore.While addressing a public gathering in Bhogapuram after the airport's inaugural ceremony, PM Modi said Andhra would emerge as a manufacturing hub under Naidu's leadership. He said the NDA government was working at "double speed" for the state's development, highlighted railway projects worth around Rs 1 lakh crore, noted that the number of airports in India had increased from 74 to 166 over the past 12 years.The Prime Minister also laid the foundation stone for Andhra Pradesh's first semiconductor manufacturing facility under the India Semiconductor Mission, which is expected to produce around 96 million semiconductor chips annually. In addition, he launched power transmission projects worth over Rs 9,900 crore to strengthen the National Grid and facilitate renewable energy integration from Kurnool and Ananthapuram.He further dedicated to the nation and laid the foundation stone for National Highway projects worth over Rs 1,880 crore, including stretches of NH-365BG, the Tadipatri Bypass on NH-67, and a high-level bridge at Lingasamudram on NH-565. According to the government, these projects will improve regional connectivity, reduce travel time between Visakhapatnam and Hyderabad, ease congestion and enhance road safety.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi on Saturday inaugurated the Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport at Bhogapuram in Andhra Pradesh's Vizianagaram district. NEW DELHI: Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah on Saturday announced an ex gratia payment of Rs 10 lakh each for the families of two migrant labourers from Chhattisgarh who were killed in a terrorist attack at a brick kiln in Kulgam district.The attack took place late on Friday evening in the Kelam area of south Kashmir, where unidentified gunmen opened fire on the workers. His uncle said Deepak had moved to Jammu and Kashmir around seven to eight months ago with his wife to work at the brick kiln in the hope of building a better future.Bhupendra, from Chhuiya village in Sarangarh-Bilaigarh district, had reached Kashmir around three months ago with his wife.The couple had left their four-year-old son in the care of his grandmother and younger sister while other family members worked as labourers in Himachal Pradesh.Chhattisgarh chief minister Vishnu Deo Sai expressed grief over the killings, describing the attack as "cowardly". He said the state government stood firmly with the bereaved families and had directed officials to coordinate with the Jammu and Kashmir administration to bring the bodies back home.
Article Summary: The attack took place late on Friday evening in the Kelam area of south Kashmir. The victims, both in their 20s, had travelled to the Valley in search of work. One of the labourers, 24-year-old Deepak Ratre, died before he could be taken to hospital.

NEW DELHI: Bringing the six-year-long trial in the murder of Intelligence Bureau staffer Ankit Sharma to a close, a Delhi court on Friday sentenced former AAP councillor Tahir Hussain and four others to life imprisonment, holding that Sharma was lynched “solely on account of his religion” during the 2020 northeast Delhi riots.Additional sessions judge Parveen Kumar Singh, however, declined the prosecution’s plea for the death penalty, ruling that while the brutality of the crime was undeniable, the prosecution had failed to prove any specific act committed by each convict during the murder.Pronouncing the sentence, Singh described the murder as one of exceptional brutality committed during the “communal violence that erupted in the wake of the protests against CAA/NRC”.The court held that the prosecution failed to prove allegations that Hussain had “aided, abetted, instigated or led the unlawful assembly”. Singh rejected the other convicts’ pleas that they were sole breadwinners. However, he did consider their educational background as a mitigating factor.On July 13, the court had convicted Hussain and four others, holding that the five were part of “a large crowd which, with animus against Hindus, had assembled...with a common object to commit rioting, loot, arson and to cause damage to the property and person of members of the Hindu community”, before murdering the IB staffer on Feb 25, 2020, whose body was later recovered from a drain.Hussain was sentenced to six months’ RI under IPC Section 188, three years under Section 153A, two years under Section 147, three years under Section 148, seven years under Section 365 and imprisonment for life under Section 302. All sentences will run concurrently. He was also fined Rs 1,000 under Section 188, Rs 20,000 each under Sections 153A, 147 and 148, Rs 50,000 under Section 365 and Rs 5 lakh under Section 302, with default sentences in case of non-payment.“The manner in which it was committed was of the utmost brutality. The victim was sucked in by the murderous mob, baying for blood... The assault was so fierce, unrelenting, and from such close quarters that even in death, the body did not immediately slump to the ground,” the judge held.The court noted that the violence did not end with Sharma’s death. His body, it observed, was strapped “like an animal”, dragged to Chand Bagh pulia and thrown into a drain. Calling it an “aggravating circumstance of immense magnitude”, the judge remarked, “As if the hatred had still not been satiated, the dead body was thereafter thrown into the nala. Therefore, the barbarity with which this horrendous murder was committed is nauseatingly sickening. ”Saying the “crime test” tilted the case towards the “rarest of rare” category, the judge weighed aggravating and mitigating circumst-ances before declining the capital punishment sought by special public prosecutor Madhukar Pandey, who maintained that the offence was part of “well-orchestrated communal violence” rather than a crime committed und-er sudden provocation.The court zoomed in on what it found to be the prosecution’s principal shortcoming — the lack of specificity regarding the individual role of each convict. Observing that “before a life is ordered to be extinguished by a judicial decree”, something more than mere membership of an unlawful assembly had to be proved, the judge held that the prosecution had failed to bridge that gap. While acknowledging the state’s contention that the use of a heavy cutting weapon reflected pre-planned and cold-blooded intent, the court said the time for drawing such inferences was long past and treated the lack of specificity as a “huge mitigation. ”Judge Singh rejected the convicts’ pleas that they were sole breadwinners and noted that the “monstrosity of the crime committed outweighs this mitigating circumstance”. At the same time, he found no material to conclude that they were beyond reform.It also noted that allegations of Hussain’s house being used as a “launchpad” for the riots were neither part of the charges framed nor specifically proved during trial. The judge also took note of the “entirely satisfactory” custodial conduct of Hussain, Kasim and Nazim, barring minor infractions by Kasim.Another mitigating factor, the court said, was the educational background of the convicts. It observed that “vested interests” had spread misinformation and whipped up a “religious frenzy”, making the uneducated co-convicts “more gullible and susceptible to such propaganda”, and held that this vulnerability to manipulation was relevant while determining the sentence.Hussain’s co-convicts were awarded life imprisonment under Section 302 IPC with a fine of Rs 25,000 each. They were also sentenced to six months under Section 188, three years under Section 153A, two years under Section 147, three years under Section 148 and seven years under Section 365 IPC, along with fines ranging from Rs 1,000 to Rs 10,000 under the respective provisions. All the sentences will run concurrently.As Hussain was being led out of the courtroom by police after the sentencing, he turned to those present and said, “High court se insaaf milega. Der aaye, lekin durust aaye.”Speaking to TOI, Ankur Sharma, brother of the IB staffer, said, “From day one, this has been a ‘rarest of rare’ case. While we appreciate that the trial court has delivered a conviction and handed down life imprisonment, true justice won’t be served until the perpetrators receive the death sentence, a demand we will aggressively pursue in the high court. The sheer brutality of the crime still haunts our family every single day; knowing he was inflicted with 51 wounds, subjected to acid, and dumped in a drain is a pain that never truly goes away. ”
Article Summary: Former AAP councillor Tahir Hussain and four others sentenced to life imprisonment. Sharma was lynched “solely on account of his religion’ during 2020 northeast Delhi riots. Prosecution failed to prove allegations that Hussain had “aided, abetted, instigated or led the unlawful assembly.

SHIMLA/PITHIRAGARH: India and China resumed traditional border trade Saturday through Lipulekh in Uttarakhand and Shipki La in Himachal Pradesh after nearly six years, restoring two key Himalayan trade routes that had remained closed since the Covid-19 pandemic.At Lipulekh in Uttarakhand's Pithoragarh district, the first batch of 16 traders and four support staff crossed into Tibet without goods as the two sides began restoring trade operations. Chinese authorities restricted the inaugural batch to 20 people, citing infrastructure constraints at the Taklakot trade mart and sought detailed personal information of all traders in advance. They also asked that priority be given to those who had participated in the last trading season in 2019.Accordingly, the traders' association selected traders whose goods had remained stranded at Taklakot after trade was suspended in 2020. "Priority was given to traders who had participated in the 2019 trading season and had left their goods at Taklakot," Dharchula SDM and district trade officer Ashish Joshi said.Meanwhile, in Himachal Pradesh, revenue minister Jagat Singh Negi flagged off the first batch of 16 Indian traders as they set off with their horses towards Shipki village in Tibet through the 3,930-metre-high Shipki La Pass.The trade, suspended since 2020 because of Covid, was scheduled to resume on June 1 but was delayed owing to security concerns and inadequate infrastructure at the trading post.Trade through Shipki La, which will remain open until Nov 30, will continue under the traditional barter system. Indian traders will be allowed to stay across the border for up to 72 hours, while the home department has cleared 53 traders after verification of their antecedents.Indian traders have been permitted to export 36 categories of goods, including dried fruits, spices, handicrafts and herbs, while Chinese traders can bring 20 categories of goods, including pashmina, wool, yak hair, sheepskin, goatskin and China clay. Officials said the overall list comprised 72 categories of tradable goods from the Indian side and 30 from the Chinese side.Negi also inaugurated the Rs 1.7 crore Chhuppan Trade Mart at Namgya village in Pooh subdivision near the international border to facilitate border trade.Replying to a demand by local traders to expand the list of tradable goods, Negi said the proposal would be placed before CM Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu and also with MEA.The routes were scheduled to reopen on June 1 but were delayed because of pending infrastructure and administrative preparations on both sides of the border. tnn(With inputs from Prem Punetha in Pithoragarh)

Article Title: Judge Ujjal Bhuyan questions SC collegium’s opacity
Article Text:
Citizens have right to know deliberations on elevation, transfer of judges: Bhuyan

NEW DELHI: SC judge Ujjal Bhuyan has questioned opacity in the collegium’s decisions on judicial appointments.“I have noticed that the last three collegium resolutions contain no reasons whatsoever. Is this a step back from the principle of transparency?” said Justice Bhuyan at a panel discussion on Saturday. “By withholding reasons, we also create space for individuals to enter the judiciary who may later describe groups of people as ‘ants’ and make other remarks that are wholly unconstitutional,” he said.To prevent the entry of such people, “there should be some discussion, there should be some reasons given”, said Justice Ujjal Bhuyan. Though the judge didn’t name anyone, the comment was an apparent reference to a remark by an Allahabad high court judge at a social event in 2024.He was speaking at the launch of the Judicial Transparency Index: Assessing Disclosure of Information by the Supreme Court and the High Courts, prepared by the Justice, Access and Lowering Delays in India (JALDI) Initiative at the Vidhi Centre for Legal Policy.The judge stressed that deliberations on the elevation and transfer of judges by the SC collegium largely remain confidential, contrary to the principle of judicial transparency.“While carrying out the next assessment on the scale of Judicial Transparency Index, I may request the JALDI team to also look into the aspect of opacity of the collegium system. Deliberations on elevation and transfer of judges remain confidential. Reasons for rejecting or deferring a recommendation are rarely disclosed in full. And the criteria applied are not codified in any publicly disclosed instrument. It is a very important issue. Citizens have a right to know what is happening in the courts. They have a right to know who would be their judges.They have a right to know judgments. These should be in the public domain”, Justice Bhuyan underlined.The report is the first systematic study assessing transparency practices across India’s higher judiciary and evaluates disclosure of information by the Supreme Court and high courts across judicial processes, institutional governance and administration, and judicial and administrative personnel.Referring to a previous collegium resolution reiterating the recommendation of senior advocate Saurabh Kirpal for appointment as a judge, Justice Bhuyan said he found the reasons recorded by the Supreme Court convincing but noted that despite more than three and a half years having passed, no appointment materialised.Key findings of the JALDI report reveal that only five high courts have published a budget on their websites for FY 2025-26 while none has published the criteria governing case allocation.Of the 813 judges in the higher judiciary, only 87 have publicly disclosed their assets even as only two high courts publish disciplinary sanction orders pertaining to district judicial officers.“The findings highlight that the level of judicial transparency varies across courts and demonstrate that while individual disclosure measures have emerged...they have not yet translated into a holistic approach...” a release from Vidhi said.
Article Summary: Justice Ujjal Bhuyan questioned opacity in the collegium’s decisions on judicial appointments. “I have noticed that the last three collegium resolutions contain no reasons whatsoever. Is this a step back from the principle of transparency?” he said.

Article Title: Monsoon hope as WMO sees an El Niño counter
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Monsoon may avoid deficient phase with positive IOD

NEW DELHI: The risk of overall monsoon rainfall being ‘below normal’ continues to loom over India due to a strengthening El Niño, but World Meteorological Organisation’s (WMO) latest monthly global seasonal climate update, released late Friday night, offered a ray of hope. It predicted the possibility of a “positive” Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD), which could offset to an extent the negative impact of El Niño.El Niño is a climatic pattern of warming of surface waters of central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean and is associated with a weak monsoon and harsher summer in India. IOD, on the other hand, has to do with the difference in sea surface temperatures between western and eastern parts of tropical Indian Ocean. It helps in formation of stronger monsoon winds.“A positive IOD is expected to develop... Combined with exceptionally warm global oceans and the likelihood of a positive IOD, the developing El Niño is expected to shape weather patterns across many parts of the world in the months ahead,” WMO said.If WMO’s forecast comes true, there is a possibility of improved rainfall conditions in south peninsular India — the region which had reported a high cumulative rainfall deficit of 22% as of Aug 1 — in particular and over many parts of the country in general.It may prevent India from slipping from ‘below normal’ phase to ‘deficient’ monsoon phase at the end of the rainy season.El Niño Southern Oscillation (ENSO) and IOD are two key factors that govern variation in monsoon rainfall. Though IMD Friday flagged the continuation of “neutral” IOD conditions through the remaining period of southwest (summer) monsoon, it, at the same time, referred to climate forecasts from some international forecasting centres suggesting that positive IOD conditions are likely to develop during Sept.
Article Summary: The risk of overall monsoon rainfall being ‘below normal’ continues to loom over India. World Meteorological Organisation’s (WMO) latest monthly global seasonal climate update, released late Friday night, offered a ray of hope. It predicted the possibility of a “positive” Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD), which could offset to an extent the negative impact of El Niño.

Article Title: Fear stalks Kashmir’s brick kilns after terrorists kill 2 migrant workers

KULGAM: Panic. Shuttered doors. Phones ringing with anxious calls from home. Brick kilns across south Kashmir ground to a halt Saturday as migrant labourers stayed indoors, rattled by the killing of two co-workers barely 2km away and wondering if they should leave — or stay and earn.Around 11am, Sunil Kumar, 34, and fellow labourer Renku Yadav stepped out of brick kiln No 515 in Hablishi village of Kulgam district to buy atta and pulses after running out of food. They had barely walked a short distance when the kiln owner chased after them, urging them to return.Fear had settled over the village after terrorists fatally shot two migrant labourers Friday evening at a brick kiln in neighbouring Kilam — killing Deepak Ratrey, 24, and Bhupendra Bhaina, 28, from Chhattisgarh.The attack raised concerns about the resurgence of targeted killings of non-native people in Kashmir. In 2022, a series of targeted attacks resulted in the deaths of at least 10 labourers.Terrorists tend to target “soft targets” such as migrant workers, who arrive in Kashmir every year between March and Nov — the seasonal workforce engaged in labour-intensive tasks on farms, construction sites and brick kilns.Kumar lives beside the kiln in a shelter built by stacking bricks without cement.The temporary rooms become home during the brick-making season.He has worked in J&K since 2007 and has spent nearly a decade at the same kiln, moulding clay bricks before they are fired. “Life has been peaceful in recent years. We work during the day, cook in the evening, listen to songs and speak to our families,” Kumar said.“We have seen such attacks in Kashmir, but what can a labourer do? We have to earn a living,” said Kumar, who came from Lucknow on July 16 with 12 more men for a monthly wage of Rs 18,000.Brick kiln owners fear a repeat of earlier years when attacks on migrant workers triggered an exodus, crippling businesses dependent on seasonal labour. “We came here for three months. We don’t think the situation is so bad that we should leave immediately,” Kumar assured.Zakir Ansari, 23, from Bareilly said he and nine men reached Kashmir in early July through a contractor. “Our family called all night worried, but we told them we were fine,” he said, adding that security personnel visited and assured their safety.Lt governor Manoj Sinha chaired a security review and directed officials to protect migrant workers. CM Omar Abdullah condemned the killings and announced Rs 10 lakh each for the victims’ families, in addition to Rs 6 lakh being provided by district administration.Political ripples followed the killings. NC president Dr Farooq Abdullah questioned why such attacks surface whenever the demand for restoration of J&K’s statehood gathers momentum, drawing sharp criticism from BJP and PDP. BJP’s Sunil Sharma called the remarks “very strange”, while PDP functionary Iltija Mufti urged that “a moment of grief shouldn’t be politicised”.
Article Summary: Terrorists killed two migrant labourers Friday evening at a brick kiln in neighbouring Kilam. The attack raised concerns about the resurgence of targeted killings of non-native people in Kashmir. In 2022, a series of targeted attacks resulted in the deaths of at least 10 labourers.

Article Title: 'Terrorists asked caste, community': Family claims Kulgam victims were 'identified' before being shot

NEW DELHI: The family of one of the two Chhattisgarh labourers killed in the terror attack in Jammu and Kashmir's Kulgam has alleged that the attackers asked the victims about their identity and religion before opening fire, echoing survivor accounts from the April 2025 Pahalgam terror attack.Deepak Ratrey, a resident of Bundeli village in Chhattisgarh's Sakti district, was among two migrant labourers killed when terrorists attacked a brick kiln in Kulgam on Friday night. Another victim was identified as 28-year-old Bhupendra Bhaina from Sarangarh-Bilaigarh district. Both had travelled to Kashmir in search of work and were employed at the brick kiln where the attack took place.Speaking to ANI, Deepak's uncle Haldhar Ratrey claimed the attackers targeted the labourers after asking about their identity. "From what we've heard, the terrorists shot him after asking about his caste and community. Look at this act by the terrorists - they went and shot him after asking his caste, firing at a labourer," he alleged.While there has been no official confirmation on this from the authorities, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge , in a post on X, also said the two labourers were "identified" before they were killed, which reflected the "cruel mindset of terrorism."The incident comes days after terrorists shot dead Jammu and Kashmir Police head constable Ashiq Hussain Qureshi in Anantnag while he was deployed on Amarnath Yatra duty. It was the first terror strike in Kashmir since the April 22, 2025 Pahalgam terror attack, in which 26 people were killed. He is survived by his wife, a one-year-old son, his widowed mother and a disabled brother.His family has appealed to the government to bring his mortal remains back to Chhattisgarh for the last rites and provide financial assistance to the bereaved family.Sakti sub-divisional magistrate Rupendra Patel said the administration was in constant touch with the family and coordinating with authorities in Jammu and Kashmir to ensure all possible assistance and expedite the transportation of Deepak's body to his native village.Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah announced an ex gratia of Rs 10 lakh each for the families of the two victims. India will not be intimidated by such hollow threats. These terrorists will soon be hunted down and will meet the same fate as their predecessors," he said.Deepak, the sole breadwinner of his family, had moved to Jammu and Kashmir around seven to eight months ago with his wife. He is survived by his elderly mother, a physically disabled younger brother, his wife and their four-month-old son.Bhupendra had arrived in Kashmir about three months ago with his wife, while their four-year-old son remained in Chhattisgarh with relatives.
Article Summary: Family of one of the two Chhattisgarh labourers killed in the terror attack in Jammu and Kashmir's Kulgam has alleged that the attackers asked the victims about their identity and religion before opening fire. NEW DELHI: Ladakh Police on Saturday registered a zero FIR against social media influencer Yogesh Parmar over the circulation of a Facebook video that allegedly contains objectionable remarks targeting Union Home Minister Amit Shah , and transferred the case to Karnataka for further investigation, officials said.The FIR was lodged at Leh police station after a written complaint alleged that a Facebook video shared through a link contained remarks that were “highly objectionable, hateful and offensive” against the home minister.The case has been registered under Sections 197(1)(d) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) relating to acts against national integration, 352 for insult intended to provoke a breach of peace, and 353(1) for public mischief, officials said.The offences carry punishments ranging from two to three years of imprisonment, along with a fine, or both, depending on the specific provision.According to the FIR, the complainant alleged that the video was likely to promote hostility and disturb public order and communal harmony.“It is alleged that the content is likely to promote hostility, disturb public order and harmony by inciting resentment among the public.The allegations prima facie disclose the commission of a cognisable offence punishable under sections 197(1)(d), 352, 353(1) of the BNS,” officials said, citing the FIR.As the alleged incident falls under the jurisdiction of the Devaraja police station in Mysuru City, Karnataka, Leh police registered a zero FIR and transferred the case to the concerned police station for further investigation, officials added.A zero FIR allows police to register a cognisable offence irrespective of where the alleged incident took place and subsequently transfer the case to the appropriate jurisdiction.

Article Title: July GST collections up 15.4% to Rs 2.1 L cr on higher imports

NEW DELHI: GST collections rose 15.4% to Rs 2,11,205 crore in July, the second highest since the new structure was implemented last Sept, on the back of a 29% jump in integrated GST (IGST) on imports. This was also the highest pace of growth since rate rationalisation.The rise in IGST on imports in July (for transactions in the previous month) may be attributed to higher prices of crude and other commodities in the wake of the West Asia conflict.The impact of strong economic activity in June, when factory output grew at its fastest pace in nearly two years, was also visible on the tax numbers, seen as an advance indicator of economic activity. Some of the price hikes in FMCG and automobile sectors would have also buoyed collections. Central GST mop-up was pegged 12.3% higher at just under Rs 40,000 crore, while state GST grew 8.7% to nearly Rs 48,000 crore."The high GST collections tie in very well with the 7.3% increase in industrial production during June. It reflects continued economic resilience despite the challenges in the external environment...Thesteady growth in GST collections each month indicates that overall domestic consumption is becoming largely insulated from seasonal variations and external headwinds," said MS Mani, partner at Deloitte India.Some experts, however, are worried about the continued rise in imports. "...one cannot ignore the elevated levels of import GST collections, which remain a nagging concern. This points to a persistent gap in domestic manufacturing capability despite the range of successful PLI and Atmanirbhar Bharat interventions rolled out over the past few years.It is likely that the sustained push by policymakers towards localisation of around 100 products (being talked about) over a period of time will help bridge this gap," said Saurabh Agarwal, partner at EY India, a consulting firm.Net of refunds, which were 13% higher at almost Rs 30,000 crore, collections went up 15.8% to Rs 1,81,237 crore.Haryana logged the highest growth of 28%, followed by Gujarat and Puducherry (26%), Karnataka and Goa (23%), and Maharashtra (20%). Chhattisgarh (23% fall), Jharkhand and Manipur (20% decline) were among the laggards.
Article Summary: GST collections rose 15.4% to Rs 2,11,205 crore in July. This was the second highest since the new structure was implemented last Sept. Haryana logged the highest growth of 28%, followed by Gujarat and Puducherry (26%) Karnataka and Goa (23%) and Maharashtra (20%)

Article Title: Cloudburst damages structures in Kishtwar; rain halts Amarnath Yatra
Article Text: JAMMU: Flash floods triggered by a cloudburst in Chatroo area of J&K’s Kishtwar district early Saturday damaged shops and houses, inundated the main market with boulders, mud and slush, damaged Kishtwar–Chatroo–Sinthan national highway, and prompted authorities to shut schools.Meanwhile, Amarnath Yatra was suspended from Jammu’s Bhagwati Nagar base camp on Saturday as Jammu–Srinagar NH remained closed for the second consecutive day due to incessant rain.“At least two vehicles parked near a local stream in Kishtwar were washed away, while four to five shops and around three houses were damaged. Article Title: NEET-PG 2026 gets major overhaul: Centres closer to home, single-shift exam, fewer questions with no change in test duration

NEW DELHI: The Centre has announced a series of changes for the NEET-PG exam to be held later in the month, including expanding the choice of test locations, giving candidates more time to plan travel, and increasing the time available per question.The reforms are aimed at making the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test for Postgraduate (NEET-PG) process more convenient and secure, according to the Union health ministry.Under the revised system, candidates will have to provide preferences for three states for their examination centre. Their correspondence state will be the mandatory first preference, allowing allotment of centres closer to their place of residence.Earlier, examination centres were allotted on a first-come, first-served basis, prompting candidates to submit applications immediately after registrations opened. Those who delayed often found nearby centres unavailable and had to travel to other states.Candidates will now be informed of their allotted test city nearly three weeks before the August 30 examination, giving them more time to arrange travel and accommodation.The National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences (NBEMS) has also revised the exam pattern, reducing the number of questions from 200 to 180 while keeping the total duration unchanged at 210 minutes. The move will provide candidates with more time per question.The exam was earlier conducted with 200 multiple-choice questions carrying a maximum of 800 marks.The ministry said the question paper preparation and delivery process has been strengthened through multiple layers of encryption, secure offline preparation, time-bound finalisation of papers shortly before the examination, and controlled digital decryption at the start of the test.To further strengthen security, Aadhaar-based authentication has been introduced during registration and on the examination day. Iris-based biometric verification will be used where fingerprint authentication fails.NBEMS has also introduced a dedicated email address for reporting impersonation, touting and other unfair practices, while issuing advisories to candidates to improve awareness and vigilance.NEET-PG 2026 will be conducted in a single shift to ensure uniformity in difficulty level and assessment. In recent years, the exam was conducted in multiple shifts due to emergencies or postponements.Union health minister JP Nadda on Saturday reviewed preparations for the examination and directed agencies to ensure a smooth, secure, transparent and technology-enabled process. He assessed the readiness of NBEMS, technology partners and other stakeholders, and stressed the need for a fair and candidate-friendly examination.A total of 2,73,183 candidates have registered for the medical entrance test, an increase of over 12.5% from last year. The exam will be held in a single shift across around 340 cities and more than 1,300 centres.Security measures include advance sealing and verification of centres, CCTV surveillance, biometric authentication, candidate frisking, deployment of signal jammers, live monitoring through central and regional command centres, and supervision by independent observers and appraisers.More than 60,000 examination functionaries will be deployed for the smooth conduct of the examination, the ministry said.
Article Summary: The reforms are aimed at making the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test for Postgraduate (NEET-PG) process more convenient and secure. Candidates will have to provide preferences for three states for their examination centre. The National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences (NBEMS) has also revised the exam pattern.

NEW DELHI: Busting a big racket on counterfeit military uniforms, a joint operation by Indian Army’s intelligence units and Rajasthan police has led to the seizure of nearly 1,000 metres of unauthorised army-pattern combat cloth from shops across the state’s Sriganganagar district.Acting on a lead, intelligence personnel of the Indian Army carried out a discrete investigation in the city, which pointed to a local firm, as a key link in the supply chain allegedly distributing counterfeit army-pattern combat cloth to shops in Sriganganagar town as well as Lalgarh Jattan, Suratgarh and other nearby markets, the Indian Army said.An interim investigation report was shared with Rajasthan police in mid-July, leading to a coordinated operation on July 30 in which security personnel and police searched multiple shops across the district. The raids yielded approximately 1,000 metres of unauthorised, new-pattern counterfeit combat cloth, exposing a wider network allegedly supplying counterfeit military uniforms to vendors in the region, the Army said.The action followed a seizure of similar counterfeit combat cloth in Bareilly in June this year, which was traced back to a manufacturing source in Sriganganagar.Radical elements and terrorists had in the past exploited open-market military fatigues to infiltrate high-security zones or stage attacks such as in Pathankot and J&K.In India, unauthorised sale, production or storage of official military-pattern camouflage cloth is heavily restricted and banned by local civil administrations in many sensitive regions. Section 168 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 punishes any civilian who unlawfully wears military uniforms or carries tokens of the Indian armed forces with the intent to trick others into believing they are a soldier, sailor or airman.Furthermore, the Indian Army holds exclusive Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) over its digital camouflage pattern design, making commercial reproduction by open-market vendors illegal.
Article Summary: A joint operation by Indian Army’s intelligence units and Rajasthan police has led to the seizure of nearly 1,000 metres of unauthorised army-pattern combat cloth. The action followed a seizure of similar counterfeit combat cloth in Bareilly in June this year.

Article Title: ‘My return to Kolkata proves injustice cannot be permanent’: Taslima Nasreen
Article Text:
Exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen in Kolkata. (PTI Photo)

NEW DELHI: Exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen on Saturday described her return to India after nearly two decades as proof that “injustice can be long but cannot be permanent. ”She made the remarks at an event in Kolkata, nearly two decades after she was forced to leave the city in 2007. The 63-year-old writer had been living in Kolkata since leaving Bangladesh in 1994 amid alleged death threats from radical groups over her writings and views on religion.Nasreen, who has been living in Europe since leaving Kolkata, also clarified that her return to the city was not linked to any "political agenda.""Today, the opening of this door proves that injustice can be long, but it cannot be permanent. History remembers who closed the doors and who opened them...I am not here to speak for any political party, or against any party. I am here to speak in favour of women's rights," PTI quoted her as saying.She also expressed concern over what she described as a "rise" in religious extremism in Bangladesh."I am against all forms of fundamentalism, but I have spoken against Islamic fundamentalists because I have seen it from close quarters since childhood.The rise of fundamentalism in Bangladesh is at an alarming stage. Freedom of speech is being curtailed," Nasreen said.Visibly emotional, Nasreen called her return a "fulfilment of a long-awaited moment.""It took me 19 years to say these words: 'I have returned to Kolkata.' I felt the pain of losing an address every single day. On August 8, 1994, the then government forced me to leave Bangladesh. The state may have removed me from my country, but it could never remove my country from within me," she added.Lamenting that she could not find a permanent home in either Bangladesh or West Bengal, Nasreen highlighted that Europe had provided her security but not a sense of belonging."Europe has given me citizenship and a place to live, but unfortunately, I couldn't get a small place to stay in the two Bengals. Europe gave me security, but it could not give me a sense of belonging. A home is not built by security alone; it is built by language, memory and culture," Nasreen remarked.Nasreen maintained that she had never been convicted by any court but had faced restrictions because of opposition from fundamentalist groups."I committed no crime. No court has ever punished me. It is a painful truth of our times that a writer needs police protection to visit the city of her own language."Rejecting allegations that her writings were offensive, she emphasised that her advocacy had focused on equality and human rights."I only spoke about equal rights for women and men, and about human rights irrespective of religion or caste. I said that any rule or doctrine that takes away equality and human dignity must be changed."She also criticised what she described as the unequal treatment of women in the name of religion and backed a Uniform Civil Code across South Asia, arguing that religion-based personal laws discriminate against women."The real conflict is between secularism and fundamentalism, between the rational mind and irrationality, between innovation and tradition, and between people who value freedom and those who do not."
Article Summary: Taslima Nasreen was forced to leave Kolkata in 1994 amid alleged death threats. The 63-year-old writer had been living in Europe since leaving the city in 2007. Nasreen said her return to the city was not linked to any "political agenda"

NEW DELHI: Congress ' internal rift in Punjab showed no signs of easing on Saturday after supporters of former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi disrupted two party programmes by raising slogans in his favour, prompting AICC general secretary in charge of Punjab Bhupesh Baghel to warn that anyone indulging in indiscipline would be expelled from the party.The slogan shouting took place during the Congress' 'Har Booth, Congress Mazboot' programmes in Patiala and Sangrur, where Baghel, Punjab Congress chief Amarinder Singh Raja Warring and several senior leaders were present.Despite the disruption, Baghel reiterated that the Congress high command would decide the party's chief ministerial face only after the Punjab Assembly elections, due early next year.The disruption began in Patiala soon after Warring started addressing party workers. Channi's supporters raised slogans including "Charanjit Singh Channi Zindabad", "Channi Teri Soch Te Pehra Deyange Thok Ke" and "Channi Liyao, Punjab Bachao", briefly bringing the programme to a halt.A visibly upset Warring repeatedly appealed to workers to maintain discipline and allow the meeting to continue but the slogan shouting persisted for some time before proceedings resumed.Senior Congress leaders, including Baghel, MP Amar Singh and Brahm Mohindra, witnessed the developments while other leaders attempted to calm the workers.Similar scenes unfolded later in Sangrur, where another group of Channi supporters raised slogans in favour of the former chief minister and against Baghel. Tensions escalated after some of Channi's supporters clashed verbally with other Congress workers.One supporter demanded that the Jalandhar MP be declared the Congress' chief ministerial face, claiming it reflected the wishes of party workers.However, Warring dismissed suggestions that Channi had orchestrated the protests."Channi did not send these people. He is our crown," Warring said in Sangrur, while alleging that the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) had sent people to disrupt the Congress programme.Addressing party workers, Baghel urged leaders to remain united and focus on defeating the ruling AAP, the BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal instead of engaging in internal rivalries.He made it clear that the Congress leadership, including party president Mallikarjun Kharge and leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, would decide the chief ministerial candidate and ministers only after the Assembly elections."Smaller differences are part of every party which can be sorted out for the bigger battle that the Congress has to fight against AAP, BJP and Akalis," Baghel said.He expressed confidence that the Congress would emerge stronger in the Assembly elections because everyone shared the common objective of bringing the party back to power in Punjab.Baghel also underlined the importance of strengthening the party at the booth level, saying a strong grassroots organisation would be key to electoral success.Later, speaking to reporters in Patiala, Baghel issued a stern warning against indiscipline."Whosoever indulges in indiscipline will be shown the door from the party irrespective of the position one holds," he said, citing the earlier expulsion of Navjot Kaur Sidhu as an example.When asked whether the party would initiate action against Channi, Baghel responded by asking what mistake the former chief minister had committed.Warring, meanwhile, announced that former MLA Madan Lal Jalalpur had been suspended for remarks against senior Congress leaders.Rejecting reports that some leaders had stayed away from district committee meetings, Baghel said all leaders had been informed about the programmes and were participating as their schedules permitted.In his address, Warring stressed that no leader, regardless of popularity, could win elections without a strong organisational structure.He cited the example of late Punjabi singer Sidhu Moosewala, saying that despite his immense popularity, he lost the 2022 Assembly election by over 60,000 votes because of inadequate booth-level management.Warring also said his only wish was to see a Congress chief minister and ministers taking oath after the next Assembly elections, adding that he would be happy to watch the swearing-in ceremony from the audience.He described senior leaders including Channi, Partap Singh Bajwa, Rajinder Kaur Bhattal and Brahm Mohindra as more experienced and capable than himself, and assured workers that all senior leaders would soon be seen sharing one platform ahead of the polls.The latest developments indicate continuing factionalism within the Punjab Congress despite repeated assurances from the party leadership that organisational unity is being strengthened ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections.Baghel is currently touring the poll-bound state as part of the 'Har Booth, Congress Mazboot' campaign, meeting district and block-level leaders after launching the initiative in Fatehgarh Sahib and Mohali on Friday.Baghel had earlier dismissed reports of factionalism, claiming that the media and a few individuals were creating a perception of infighting.However, discontent within the state unit has continued since the Congress retained Amarinder Singh Raja Warring as Punjab Congress president while appointing Channi as chairman of the campaign committee.A section of leaders led by Channi and Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa had opposed Warring's continuation as state chief and sought his removal.
Article Summary: Channi supporters disrupt Congress meetings in Patiala and Sangrur. AICC general secretary in charge of Punjab Bhupesh Baghel warns against indiscipline. Baghel says the party's chief ministerial face will be decided after polls.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday ruled that a wife cannot be granted interim maintenance if an allegation of adultery is made against her which, at first glance, looks true.A bench of Justices Sanjay Karol and Vipul M Pancholi quashed the order of the Rajasthan High Court which had held that a wife cannot be denied interim maintenance during pendency of the husband’s application under Section 125(4) of the Criminal Procedure Code relating to adultery. It allowed the plea of a husband who approached the court through lawyer Prabhjit Jauhar against the orders of a trial court and HC rejecting his plea to examine allegations of adultery before granting interim maintenance.“It is obvious that when a case is sought to be proved by circumstantial evidence, it requires a detailed study of the circumstances presented. The evidence furnished in support thereof, including verification, particularly when the evidence in question is electronic, etc. These procedures are bound to take time. Since the stipulation in Section 125 (4) is that if adultery is proved, the wife would neither be entitled to interim nor final maintenance, we are of the view that if a husband files an application under Section 125(4) and is, at the first instance, able to establish the charge through evidence ex facie, then only, there can be said to be a bar to interim maintenance,” the bench said.It added that the trial court and HC clearly fell into error to hold that it was only at the stage of final adjudication that such a question could be decided. “This view would render otiose what has been provided in the statute,” it said.Section 125(4) says that no wife shall be entitled to receive an allowance for maintenance or interim maintenance and expenses of proceedings, as the case may be, from her husband if she is living in adultery, or if, without any sufficient reason, she refuses to live with her husband, or if they are living separately by mutual consent.“If the application for maintenance is to be denied at the interim stage itself, the party having filed the application under Section 125(4) must present clear and cogent evidence that would ex-facie establish adultery on the part of the claimant for maintenance,” the bench said.Noting that the husband in the case has placed a large number of photographs and 92 videos to substantiate his allegation against the wife, the court said they were perhaps procured from a private detective and expressed the need to frame a law to regulate the sector as there was an increasing reliance on private investigators to gather information.“We believe that regulation and accountability are equally important in the sphere of private investigation,” it said
Article Summary: A bench of Justices Sanjay Karol and Vipul M Pancholi quashed the order of the Rajasthan High Court. It allowed the plea of a husband who approached the court through lawyer Prabhjit Jauhar against the orders of a trial court and HC.

Article Title: DMK moves SC seeking immediate release of Cauvery water from Karnataka to Tamil Nadu
Article Text:
Responding to the growing protests in Karnataka, chief minister DK Shivakumar appealed on Saturday to organisations opposing the release of water to withdraw their proposed agitation.

NEW DELHI: The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) on Saturday moved the Supreme Court seeking directions to the Karnataka government to immediately release Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu, arguing that Karnataka must comply with the apex court's 2018 verdict and the recent directions issued by the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA).The plea seeks an order directing Karnataka to implement the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee's recommendation, upheld by the CWMA on Thursday, to release 3,500 cusecs of water per day for 15 days to Tamil Nadu at the inter-state border point of Biligundlu."Direct the State of Karnataka / Respondent No. 1 to forthwith and fully implement the direction of the CWRC dated July 28, 2026, as affirmed by the CWMA on July 30, 2026, by ensuring a flow of 3,500 cusecs per day at Biligundlu for the period of 15 days commencing from date of the order passed by this Hon'ble Court, and to make good the shortfall in compliance from July 29, 2026 onwards," the DMK said in its plea.The party also sought a direction to Karnataka to clear the accumulated shortfall in water releases. It asked the court to direct the state to "make good the accumulated backlog of about 9.46 TMC due at Biligundlu as on July 26, 2026, computed on the pro-rata/distress-sharing basis, by ensuring releases such that about 7,000 cusecs per day is realised at Biligundlu over a period of 15 days".In addition, the DMK urged the Supreme Court to direct the CWMA to monitor reservoir releases in Karnataka and the flows realised at Biligundlu on a day-to-day basis and submit compliance reports.The move comes amid renewed tensions between the two southern states over the sharing of Cauvery waters during the current monsoon season. On Thursday, the CWMA upheld the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee's recommendation that Karnataka release 3,500 cusecs of water daily for the next 15 days to Tamil Nadu.Responding to the growing protests in Karnataka, chief minister DK Shivakumar appealed on Saturday to organisations opposing the release of water to withdraw their proposed agitation. The farmer groups and pro-Kannada organisations staged demonstrations across the Cauvery basin, arguing that the state could not spare even a drop of water for Tamil Nadu because major reservoirs did not have enough water even for drinking.Shivakumar said the Kabini reservoir was rapidly filling up and warned that water could not be retained once the reservoir reached full capacity."Kabini reservoir is filling up. Once a dam is full, water has to be released. It is impossible to hold it back. I humbly appeal to those planning to agitate against the release of water to withdraw their decision," he said.Shivakumar also cautioned protesters against approaching water release points, saying, "Even if we decide not to release water, once the reservoir is full, it is impossible to hold it back. Protesters should not go near the points where water is being released. The force of the water can sweep you away. No one should lie down in the path of flowing water."The Karnataka CM said the state would protect the interests of its farmers while respecting judicial orders. "There is an order to release 177 TMC of water to Tamil Nadu, and the Supreme Court has upheld it. We must respect the court's order while also protecting the interests of our farmers. Our government is committed to safeguarding the welfare of Karnataka's farmers," he said.He also accused the BJP of "politicising" the issue and said an all-party meeting would be held to consult former chief ministers, political leaders and legal experts before deciding the state's next course of action. According to Shivakumar, Tamil Nadu had sought 9,000 cusecs, but the Authority had directed Karnataka to release only 3,500 cusecs.The Cauvery Water Management Authority was constituted by the Centre in 2018 following the Supreme Court's final verdict on the decades-old Cauvery river water dispute among Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala and Puducherry. The Authority includes representatives of the riparian states as well as a nominee of the central government and is responsible for overseeing implementation of the court-mandated water-sharing arrangement.
Article Summary: The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) on Saturday moved the Supreme Court seeking directions to the Karnataka government to immediately release Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu. The party argues that Karnataka must comply with the apex court's 2018 verdict and the recent directions issued by the Cauved Water Management Authority. The move comes amid renewed tensions between the two southern states over the sharing of Cauvey waters.

Article Title: ‘Egg-therapy could turn on its head’: Bengal BJP chief Samik Bhattacharya cautions party workers
Article Text:
BJP West Bengal president and Rajya Sabha MP Samik Bhattacharya (File photo)
