(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: BJP's West Bengal unit president Samik Bhattacharya on Saturday cautioned party workers against becoming arrogant, warning that the infamous "egg therapy" could otherwise "turn on its head. ""No system can function or be made to live for long by quashing protests. All autocracies across the world inevitably fall. If someone from our side sports a body language of having 207 MLAs and hits the road, then the consequence will be disastrous," he said at event in Kolkata, referring to the number seats the BJP won in the assembly elections in April to form its first government in the state.“The unwarranted egg therapy we see now can turn on its head and start falling on the other side as well. Everyone, including those in my party, must understand that. Those ‘Sanatanis’ who have suddenly found a place in our party and are harbouring aspirations for influence and advantage must also remain careful because the trajectory of those eggs can change in no time,” the Rajya Sabha MP remarked, apparently referring to leaders who joined the BJP from the Trinamool Congress (TMC), which lost power in West Bengal after 15 years.The “egg therapy” Bhattacharya mentioned alluded to incidents of egg-pelting targeting TMC leaders after the party's defeat.He also acknowledged that despite having assumed political power in West Bengal, the BJP has not yet been entirely successful in eradicating the "culture of extortion.""Our government has come to power only two months ago. We have not been able to solve all problems. If I say that we have been able to eradicate extortion from everywhere, then I will be making a false claim.There are deviations. People had become accustomed to passing through a system of making easy money through syndicates. Not everything has changed with the change in state power," Bhattacharya told the audience."Some joined the ruling party (BJP) within four hours, others had dormant wishes that have now surfaced. We are trying to control such tendencies within the party. Our CM Suvendu Adhikari is also trying to apply strict brakes on such tendencies."Emphasising the need to free the business ecosystem from "partisan politics," the BJP leader argued that West Bengal stood at the "cusp of breaking with its chequered industrial past.""We must keep partisan politics out of this system. We have become residents of a political society in West Bengal. We need freedom from it. Till such time Bengal is able to come out of the culture of infiltration of politics in every sphere of life, no government can bring about its effective change and attract investment.""We are making an earnest effort to build a government for West Bengal."Bhattacharya described the BJP's progress towards that goal as only a "partial success.""We haven't been able to provide you with an error-free atmosphere, but we have largely been able to deliver an investment climate that is fear-free. To set up a company, you can now buy your own brick, cement and sand. If someone approaches you, use the phone. He will either leave your premises or find himself inside a lock-up."
Article Summary: BJP's West Bengal unit president Samik Bhattacharya cautioned party workers against becoming arrogant. He warned that the infamous "egg therapy" could otherwise "turn on its head" He also acknowledged that despite having assumed political power in West Bengal, the BJP has not yet been entirely successful in eradicating the "culture of extortion"

Article Title: CBI books Anil Ambani, Reliance Capital in Rs 1,816 crore EPFO fraud case
Article Text:
CBI books Anil Ambani, Reliance Capital in Rs 1,816 crore EPFO fraud case

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

MUMBAI: The CBI on Saturday registered a cheating case against Reliance Capital Ltd (RCL), its ex-chairman Anil Ambani and unknown public servants over the alleged Rs 1,816 crore loss caused to the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO).The agency alleged that the EPFO invested in RCL’s secured non-convertible debentures, on which the company subsequently defaulted on repayment.Earlier, the issue was settled before the NCLT, but recently the Enforcement Directorate (ED) shared its investigation finding of RCL’s fraudulent translations. Based on this, the EPFO inquired into the issue and subsequently filed the fraud case against Ambani and RCL with the CBI.A spokesperson of Anil Ambani said, “The FIR registered by the CBI pertains to Reliance Capital Limited. Mr Ambani served as a non-executive director/chairman of the board of Reliance Capital Limited from 2005 until November 2021, when the Reserve Bank of India superseded the board of directors of the company and appointed an administrator. Mr Ambani denies any wrongdoing, whatsoever, and reserves all rights available to him in law.EPFO administered the Employees’ Provident Fund, Pension Scheme and Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme. The fund accumulations with EPFO were vested in the Central Board of Trustees (CBT), the statutory governing body which held, managed and invests such funds in trust for benefit of the subscribers.During 2013-14, RCL issued secured NCD and portfolio manager of EPFO had invested Rs 2,500 crore in it. The maturity period was in 2023-24. RCL’s financial position deteriorated in 2019, and the company subsequently went into the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process.In 2021, the EPFO lodged its claim before the Resolution Professional and, after NCLT approval in 2024, the EPFO received Rs 1,492 crore of its total dues. The remaining amount of Rs 1007 crore, along with Rs 809 crore interest, remained unpaid.The ED, which investigated RCL in a separate case, recently shared its findings with the EPFO.Citing the ED findings and documentary evidence recovered during the investigation, the EPFO said in its complaint to the CBI that “the conduct of and transactions entered into Reliance Capital Limited and the persons in charge of its management during the period 7 December 2019 to 6 December 2021 disclose various fraudulent transactions. In addition, during earlier period as well, various fraudulent transactions have been found which also led to ultimate failure of RCL as a consequence of siphoning off of money of RCL. ”
Article Summary: CBI registered a cheating case against Reliance Capital Ltd (RCL), its ex- chairman Anil Ambani and unknown public servants. The agency alleged that the EPFO invested in RCL’s secured non-convertible debentures on which the company subsequently defaulted on repayment.

Article Title: West Bengal to clear all pending CAA applications within six months, says Suvendu Adhikari
Article Text:
File photo: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari

Nearly 24,000 citizenship certificates issued so far

'CAA was never meant to target anyone'

TMC accused of spreading confusion over CAA

Government to assist beneficiaries

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Census exercise and refugee distinction

NEW DELHI: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Saturday announced that all pending applications for citizenship under the Citizenship (Amendment) Act (CAA) in the state would be disposed of within the next six months, asserting that the law was enacted to grant citizenship and not to take it away.Speaking at a CAA citizenship certificate distribution programme in New Town, where around 300 members of the Matua community from North 24 Parganas district received citizenship certificates, Adhikari alleged that the previous Trinamool Congress (TMC) government had spread misinformation about the law for "political gains"."The CAA is meant to grant citizenship, not to take away anyone's citizenship," Adhikari said, as quoted by news agency PTI.He urged all eligible applicants to come forward and apply under the Act, saying more citizenship certificates would be issued in the coming months.Presenting the state's progress in implementing the CAA, Adhikari said 23,956 citizenship certificates had been issued so far, including 5,966 certificates over the past 11 weeks since the BJP government assumed office.According to him, the state has received 2,30,605 applications under the CAA.He said Nadia district has recorded the highest number of beneficiaries with 10,191 citizenship certificates, followed by North 24 Parganas with 8,930 certificates.Adhikari also said that, following discussions with the Union home secretary, the process of delegating legal and administrative powers to district magistrates for the speedy disposal of CAA applications is expected to begin within a month."Following discussions with the Union home secretary, the process of delegating legal and administrative powers to district magistrates for the speedy disposal of CAA applications is expected to begin within a month," he said.He noted that district magistrates in Gujarat and Rajasthan already exercise such powers.The chief minister reiterated that the Citizenship (Amendment) Act was introduced to grant Indian citizenship to eligible refugees and not to deprive anyone of their rights.The CAA, passed by Parliament in 2019, provides a pathway to Indian citizenship for Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis and Christians who fled religious persecution in Pakistan, Bangladesh and Afghanistan and entered India on or before December 31, 2014.Recalling the BJP's promise on citizenship, Adhikari said Prime Minister Narendra Modi had assured members of the Matua community before the 2019 Lok Sabha elections that eligible refugees from Bangladesh would receive Indian citizenship.He said the rules under the Act were eventually notified on March 6, 2024, after implementation was delayed due to the Covid-19 pandemic.Targeting the previous TMC government, Adhikari alleged that it deliberately equated the CAA with the National Register of Citizens (NRC), creating confusion among people, particularly Muslims."The previous government projected the CAA as the NRC and misled the people, particularly the Muslim community. False propaganda was spread claiming that applying under the CAA would result in the loss of jobs, ration benefits or the Lakshmir Bhandar financial assistance scheme," he alleged.He claimed that government property had been vandalised during protests triggered by such misinformation and said, "Today, the truth has come out, and even MLAs from the opposition have attended this government programme voluntarily."Adhikari said the state government would take steps to help eligible CAA beneficiaries who continue to face legal proceedings or remain in jail because of documentation-related issues by facilitating their release on bail.He added that the state police had been instructed to ensure that no eligible applicant faced harassment in matters related to the CAA.The state government will also facilitate the inclusion of beneficiaries' names in electoral rolls after citizenship is granted and ensure that eligible applicants receive Scheduled Caste certificates in a time-bound manner.One of the beneficiaries, a woman refugee originally from Bagerhat in Bangladesh, thanked the government after receiving her citizenship certificate."I lived in Bagerhat in Bangladesh and came to India in 2006. I had been living in fear for so many years. I thank the Prime Minister and the chief minister," she said, as cited by PTI.The announcement comes as West Bengal began the self-enumeration phase of the country's 16th Census.Adhikari had said the Census exercise and illegal immigration were separate issues, while distinguishing between illegal immigrants and refugees covered under the CAA.He had maintained that refugees eligible under the CAA would be protected, while illegal immigrants would not be entitled to government welfare benefits.He also said the Census would help create a permanent database for delivering government welfare schemes more efficiently.
Article Summary: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari says all pending applications for citizenship under the Citizenship (Amendment) Act (CAA) in the state will be disposed of within the next six months. The CAA, passed by Parliament in 2019, provides a pathway to Indian citizenship for Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis and Christians.

Article Title: India’s students do not need PM Modi's forgiveness, they are owed his apology: Rahul Gandhi
Article Text:
File photo: PM Modi and leader of opposition in Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi

NEW DELHI: Reacting sharply to Prime Minister Narendra Modi 's late night Instagram video on Friday, Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi while citing leaked papers, cancelled exams and years of hard work of students destroyed in the process, lashed out at the PM for having the "audacity" to speak of “forgiving” students. "India’s students do not need his forgiveness. They are owed his apology," Gandhi said.In an Instagram video posted on Friday night PM said that he will forgive young protesters accused of abusing him and his late mother, saying they are misguided children and it is “our job to show them the right way”.“Nothing is more painful than seeing a parent grieve their child. Behind every young life lost is a family carrying pain that will never leave them - and serious questions about a broken education system,” Gandhi said in a post on X where he also shared images of his interaction with parents and students.“Leaked papers. Cancelled exams. Years of preparation destroyed overnight. Our students are told to work honestly in a system that is not honest with them. And the Prime Minister has the audacity to speak of “forgiving” students,” Gandhi added.Alleging that the PM has not met a single grieving parent and has not sat with a single student whose future was stolen by a leaked paper, Gandhi said that the students don’t need Modi’s forgiveness rather “they are owed his apology”.Reacting sharply to the PM”s video, Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said in a post on X that the “PM enjoys playing the victim card” and added that Modi’s “InstaGram Sabhas are fooling no one”.“Late last night, in an act of supreme self-obsession, the PM said that he forgave our youth. This is an insult to the nation and to our youth which has suffered under his govt and is legitimately demanding an apology from him,” Ramesh said.The Congress leader went on to accuse the PM of using “vile vitriol against his predecessors and political opponents”. “He very frequently peddles lies to defame them, not just in his public speeches but in Parliament itself. He unleashes an army of foul-mouthed abusers both in Parliament and outside and gives them full protection,” Ramesh alleged.The Congress leader said that “the entire nation is wanting the PM to apologise for the trauma suffered by the youth due to paper leaks and the brutality unleashed on student protesters. Ramesh also raised the donation theft by Ram Temple Trust in Ayodhya.“The entire nation is waiting for the PM to apologise for the ‘Chanda Chori Astha Dhoka’ by the Ram Mandir Trust, an establishment which he had grandly announced in the Lok Sabha on February 5, 2020,” he added.Ramesh further said that “the entire nation is still expecting his apology for his Tughlakian decision of Nov 8 2016 that destroyed crores of livelihoods and shuttered lakhs if MSMEs. The list is endless.”
Article Summary: Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi lashed out at the PM for having the "audacity" to speak of "forgiving" students. "India’s students do not need his forgiveness. They are owed his apology," Gandhi said. PM said that he will forgive young protesters accused of abusing him and his late mother.
